question: The unit digit of 7¹⁰³ is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cyclicity of base digit 7 is 4 (7, 9, 3, 1).

Divide exponent 103 by cyclicity 4.

103 ÷ 4 ⇒ Remainder = 3.

Unit digit = 7³ = 343 → 3.

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Expression is 7¹⁰³

Method: Unit digit calculation using cyclicity of powers.

⇒ 7¹ = 7 (Unit digit: 7)

⇒ 7² = 49 (Unit digit: 9)

⇒ 7³ = 343 (Unit digit: 3)

⇒ 7⁴ = 2401 (Unit digit: 1)

⇒ 7⁵ = 16807 (Unit digit: 7)

⇒ Since the unit digit repeats every 4 powers, cyclicity = 4.

⇒ Divide 103 by 4: 103 = (25 × 4) + 3

⇒ Unit digit of 7¹⁰³ = Unit digit of 7³

⇒ 7³ = 343

⇒ Required unit digit = 3

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclicity of Digits

Digits 0, 1, 5, 6 have cyclicity 1. Digits 4 and 9 have cyclicity 2. Digits 2, 3, 7, 8 have cyclicity 4.

Zero Remainder Rule

If the remainder of Exponent ÷ Cyclicity is 0, the unit digit is the same as baseCyclicity. For example, unit digit of 7¹⁰⁰ is 7⁴ → 1.

BODMAS in Unit Digits

When finding unit digits of sums or products, perform operations only on the unit digits of individual terms to save time.</p
